content.title: SF awash in green as Irish pride overflows at St. Patrick’s Day Parade
content.text: A group with bagpipes marches along San Francisco’s Market Street during the 175th annual St. Patrick’s Day Parade on Saturday. The parade is one of the longest-running St. Patrick’s Day celebrations in the nation. Benjamin Fanjoy/For the S.F. ChronicleUnder a hot afternoon sun, thousands of spectators dressed in shades of bright shamrock and deep emerald lined the streets of downtown San Francisco on Saturday for the city’s annual St. Patrick’s Day Parade.Now in its 175th year, the parade — one of the longest-running St. Patrick’s Day celebrations in the United States — made its way along Market Street from Second Street to Civic Center. Irish bagpipers, marching bands, and dancers mingled in a procession of community groups, unions and cultural organizations honoring the city’s Irish heritage. Revelers in sparkling green fedoras, dogs in leprechaun hats and people with hair dyed bright green watched the parade pass in glee.Article continues below this adGet Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.Get Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.ONLY 25¢Sean Reilly, 60, of Medford, Ore., waved an Irish flag as his dog, Clancy, wagged his tail nearby, wearing a necklace adorned with a green beer mug.Reilly drove to San Francisco specifically for the parade, an event he hasn’t witnessed since he was a child. Both of his parents immigrated from Ireland to the United States in search of a better life. Reilly has returned to Ireland about five times and plans to go back in August.“I get goose bumps hearing bagpipes and whatnot,” he said. “I love the bagpipes. I love the drums. Just a lot of Irish pride.”A crowd gathers Saturday for San Francisco’s 175th annual St. Patrick’s Day Parade, which also marks the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States.Benjamin Fanjoy/For the S.F. ChronicleAlong the parade route, participants tossed green shamrock necklaces, candy and stickers to children reaching their hands out over the barricade. Joey D’Urso, 4, reached out for a prize and received a bounty, including a necklace, lollipop and sticker.Article continues below this adSan Francisco Chronicle LogoMake us a Preferred Source to get more of our news when you search.Add Preferred SourceHis mother, Katie D’Urso, took him out to experience Irish culture. The D’Ursos are of Irish descent and Katie, 45, of Mill Valley grew up dancing in the St. Patrick’s Day parade in Washington, D.C. Joey’s grandmother, Mo Gannon, 72, of Washington, D.C., joined the family from the East Coast.“I love the bagpipers and the dancers personally,” Katie said. “He’s excited about the sirens and any police and fire that come through, and, of course, the candy throwing.”This year’s celebration, organized by the United Irish Societies of San Francisco, also carried a broader historic note, marking the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States.Participants prepare for San Francisco’s 175th annual St. Patrick’s Day Parade, which wound its way up Market Street from Second Street to Civic Center, site of a festival.Benjamin Fanjoy/For the S.F. Chronicle“Come join us as we march down Market Street to right here in Civic Center celebrating all that is Irish in our great city,” San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie said in a social media video ahead of the parade. “Let’s go, San Francisco.”Article continues below this adHeather Harris, 54, of San Bruno made several green Amazon purchases in the days leading up to the parade. Harris bought a lime green tutu and dark green wig for herself and purchased green sweatpants, a green, curly wig and matching hat for her boyfriend.“We love going and doing, and so anytime we can get out and get crazy and like, have a good time, we’re like, all about it,” said Harris, who is of Irish and Scottish descent.Several politicians took part in the parade, including Lurie, District Attorney Brooke Jenkins, state Sen. Scott Wiener, and Assembly Members Matt Haney and Catherine Stefani. Lurie wore a green tie and stopped to shake hands with his constituents as he traveled down the parade route.Members of a contingent wave to the crowd watching the 175th annual St. Patrick’s Day Parade along Market Street in San Francisco.Benjamin Fanjoy/For the S.F. ChronicleYoung adults dressed in green packed Civic Center by the early afternoon as the sound of an accordion and a fiddle filled the air. From the back of an all terrain vehicle, a parade participant released a stream of bubbles, and the crowd burst into cheers as bagpipers and drummers marched into the plaza.Article continues below this adCivic Center hosted a free festival through the afternoon, featuring live Irish music, dances and cultural performances. Children had the chance to play traditional Irish sports, including rugby and lacrosse-like games of hurling and camogie.The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency closed several streets to traffic and rerouted Muni buses along the parade route from 10 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. It advised taking the Market Street subway or BART to the parade.San Francisco Chronicle LogoWake up to a rundown of top headlines.March 14, 2026|Updated March 14, 2026 4:37 p.m.Staff writerBrooke Park is a Hearst Fellow covering news for the San Francisco Chronicle. She spent the first year of her fellowship at San Antonio Express-News. She can be reached at Brooke.Park@hearst.com.
